items.text: OilPrice.com, Gulf Business, Reuters, Business Standard (June 8): Iran fired a salvo of missiles at Israeli targets overnight, warning against Israeli military actions in Lebanon. Israel's military said all were intercepted. Israel then retaliated: the IDF confirmed it struck 'several targets' at the Mahshahr petrochemical complex in Khuzestan Province, southwest Iran — the first direct Israeli strike on an Iranian energy facility since the April 8 ceasefire. Israel also struck Ramat David air base area targets and other military sites in western and central Iran. Iran's state media confirmed enemy projectiles hit five production lines at Mahshahr. Brent spiked to $97.15 (+4.47%) in early Asian Monday trade before settling at $94.25. WTI settled at $91.30. Brent's intraday range was $93-$97+. The Mahshahr strike is strategically significant: it is the first Israeli energy infrastructure hit since ceasefire — crossing the line Trump had tried to hold.

items.text: Washington Times, Express Tribune, Iran International (June 8): Trump posted on Truth Social: 'Israel and Iran must immediately stop shooting immediately.' In a separate post: 'Both sides, Israel and Iran, are looking to do an immediate CEASEFIRE!' Trump also told media that Netanyahu 'doesn't call the shots,' and reports confirmed Trump had rebuked Netanyahu with obscenities in a phone call last week over Israeli strikes on Lebanon and the Mahshahr hit. The Trump administration received messages from Iran stating willingness to stop shooting if Israel did the same (Axios). Iran's UN ambassador said he hopes Tehran and Washington will reach a final agreement soon. These combined signals — Trump pressure on Israel + Iran de-escalation willingness + pause in strikes (AP, Jun 8 4:49PM ET) — create the most positive deal signal since the conflict began. The question is whether Israel holds back.

items.bold: PAKISTAN DIPLOMACY: PM Shehbaz Sharif: ceasefire 'tenuous.' Interior Minister Naqvi visited Tehran, delivered special letter to Supreme Leader Khamenei. IRAN-ISRAEL APPEAR TO PAUSE STRIKES (AP, Jun 8 4:49PM ET).
items.text: Express Tribune, Iran International, AP (June 8): Pakistan's Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif said the surge in violence is a reminder that the ceasefire is 'tenuous' and that breaking it can have 'unbearable consequences,' urging all sides to exercise restraint and 'give peace a little more chance.' Pakistan's Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi visited Tehran on Saturday/Sunday, delivered a 'special letter' to Iran's Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei according to Iranian state television, then returned to Pakistan. The Naqvi letter likely contained a specific de-escalation proposal from Pakistan — the key ceasefire mediator. AP reported at 4:49PM ET June 8 that Israel and Iran appeared to pause strikes after trading fire for the first time since the April ceasefire. The pause + Naqvi letter + Trump pressure on Netanyahu = the most active mediation push since Week 12.

items.bold: IRAN AMBASSADOR TO MOSCOW: Hormuz will be open but under Iran-Oman conditions + transit fee. OPEC+ agreed +188,000 bpd for July. US redirected 129 vessels (+2). CENTCOM denied Iran fired on US destroyers.
items.text: Reuters, Gulf Business, Iran International (June 8): Iran's ambassador to Moscow stated that the Strait of Hormuz will be open but under new conditions to be set by Iran and Oman, including a transit fee — confirming Iran's PGSA toll model remains Iran's position even amid de-escalation. OPEC+ agreed to another output increase of 188,000 bpd for July, continuing its gradual rollback — but analysts say this cannot offset Hormuz closure. CENTCOM said Iran's IRGC had NOT fired on US destroyers (USS Truxtun + USS Lynde McCormick) — the Iranian claim was false. US blockade: 129 commercial vessels redirected, up 2 in the last 24 hours. Six ships disabled to ensure compliance, most recently M/T Lexie. Blockade continues in full force per Trump: 'The Blockade will remain in place, and in full force and effect until an agreement is reached, certified, and signed.'

items.bold: DEAL SIGNAL: Iran willing to stop if Israel stops. Trump pushing Netanyahu hard. Pause in strikes (AP Jun 8). Pakistan Naqvi special letter to Khamenei. Iran UN ambassador optimistic. Most positive deal environment since Day 86.
items.text: Iran International, Reuters, AP (June 8): The combination of signals heading into Day 101 creates the most positive deal environment in weeks: (1) Iran told Trump admin it is willing to stop shooting if Israel does same. (2) Trump told Netanyahu 'doesn't call the shots' + rebuked him with obscenities. (3) Israel-Iran appear to pause strikes (AP, Jun 8 4:49PM ET). (4) Pakistan PM Sharif + Naqvi special letter to Khamenei = active mediation. (5) Iran UN ambassador: hopes final agreement soon. (6) Iran ambassador Moscow: Hormuz will open (under Iran-Oman conditions). The key risk: Netanyahu defied Trump once already with the Mahshahr strike. If Israel strikes again, the fragile de-escalation collapses. The deal timeline remains mid-June at the earliest — but Tuesday's modest GIFT Nifty gap (-20 pts vs Monday's -273) suggests markets are pricing in the de-escalation. Brent closed at $94.25, not $97 — reflecting the same calculus.

military.d: OilPrice.com, Business Standard, Gulf Business (June 8): Israel's IDF confirmed it struck 'several targets' at the Mahshahr petrochemical complex in Khuzestan Province, southwest Iran — the first direct strike on an Iranian energy facility since the April 8 ceasefire. Iran's state media confirmed five production lines were hit. Israel also struck Ramat David air base area and military targets in western and central Iran. Iran had fired a salvo of dozens of missiles toward Israel overnight — all intercepted by Israeli military, no casualties. The sequence: Iran missiles at Israel → Israel strikes Mahshahr petrochemical + military targets → Trump erupts at Netanyahu. The Mahshahr plant is one of Iran's major petrochemical facilities; Iranian state media previously reported enemy projectiles hit five of its production lines since the war began. Netanyahu's decision to strike an energy facility defied explicit Trump requests to refrain — Trump had told Netanyahu not to retaliate and rebuked him with obscenities in a phone call last week.

military.t: TRUMP: 'Israel and Iran Must Immediately Stop Shooting.' + 'Both Sides Looking to Do Immediate CEASEFIRE!' Iran Told Trump Admin: Willing to Stop if Israel Stops. IRAN-ISRAEL APPEAR TO PAUSE (AP Jun 8 4:49PM).
military.d: Washington Times, Iran International, AP (June 8): Trump posted on Truth Social two pivotal messages: 'Israel and Iran must immediately stop shooting immediately' and 'Both sides, Israel and Iran, are looking to do an immediate CEASEFIRE!' Trump added he was optimistic both sides would back off. Iran told the Trump administration it is willing to stop shooting if Israel does the same (Axios). Iran's UN ambassador said he hopes Tehran and Washington will reach a final agreement soon. The AP reported at 4:49 PM ET June 8 that Israel and Iran 'appear to pause strikes after trading fire for the first time since April ceasefire.' Pakistan PM Shehbaz Sharif urged restraint, noting the final objective of a deal is 'just about to be achieved.' Pakistan Interior Minister Naqvi visited Tehran, delivered a special letter to Supreme Leader Khamenei. These combined signals represent the most active de-escalation push of the conflict. Markets are pricing this: GIFT Nifty -20 pts Tuesday (vs Monday -273), Brent close $94.25 (vs intraday $97+).

military.t: PAKISTAN NAQVI DELIVERED SPECIAL LETTER TO KHAMENEI. PM Shehbaz: Ceasefire 'Tenuous' but Final Objective 'Just About to Be Achieved.' Iran-Oman Hormuz Model: Open Under New Conditions + Transit Fee.
military.d: Express Tribune, Iran International (June 8): Pakistan's Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi visited Tehran over the weekend, delivered a 'special letter' from Pakistan (likely Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif) to Iran's Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei according to Iranian state television, then returned to Pakistan. Pakistan PM Shehbaz said: 'As we work earnestly and painstakingly, together with our brothers and partners, to find a peaceful diplomatic solution to the conflict, and especially when the final objective is just about to be achieved, we sincerely urge all sides to exercise restraint and give peace a little more chance.' The phrase 'final objective is just about to be achieved' is the strongest positive deal signal from Pakistan since Day 86 (Trump 'largely negotiated'). Iran's ambassador to Moscow stated Hormuz will be open under new Iran-Oman conditions including a transit fee — consistent with Iran's PGSA framework but signalling openness to formalising the arrangement. OPEC+ agreed to +188,000 bpd for July — limited supply relief.

DAY 91 FRI 9:15AM IST — LAST DAY OF MAY 2026. BRENT $92.56 (6:35AM ET) — DOWN 19% IN MAY. WORST MONTHLY BRENT LOSS SINCE COVID-19 PANDEMIC. Off 20% from 2026 peaks. TRUMP'S FOUR MOU CONDITIONS (CNBC confirmed): (1) Iran never have nuclear weapon. (2) Immediately open Hormuz UNRESTRICTED + WITHOUT TOLLS. (3) REMOVE remaining mines. (4) Allow US to UNEARTH AND DESTROY enriched uranium buried under rubble. Trump HAS NOT SIGNED MOU. UBS (Thursday note): "little evidence of short-term improvement in vessel traffic or energy flows." Crude loadings inside Gulf "EXTREMELY LOW." US GAS PRICES: fell 14 CENTS since $4.56/gallon peak — biggest one-day drop since November 2008 Great Recession. IRAN: will only discuss nuclear clauses ONCE Phase 1 MOU cemented. BESSENT: declined to confirm deal details. Thursday: Iran ballistic missiles toward Kuwait intercepted. IRGC warning shots at 4 vessels. India: Brent $92 = Rs 2.3L Cr annual import bill saving vs April $126 peak. OMC near-breakeven on petrol. Month-end Friday. West Asia War Day 91.

DAY 90 THU 8:15AM IST. 60-DAY MOU REACHED BY NEGOTIATORS — extend ceasefire + start nuclear negotiations. TRUMP STILL HAS TO APPROVE. Axios confirmed. CNBC confirmed. IRAN STATE TV: Tehran agreed draft MOU — Hormuz to pre-war levels — BUT Iran AND OMAN manage traffic. WHITE HOUSE: "COMPLETE FABRICATION." TRUMP: "no nation will control shipping" through Hormuz. US-IRAN EXCHANGED FIRE EARLY THURSDAY (CNN 16min ago): US struck Iranian drones + launch site near Hormuz. IRGC fired WARNING SHOTS at FOUR VESSELS near Hormuz (passing "without prior coordination or authorization"). IRAN launched BALLISTIC MISSILES TOWARD KUWAIT — intercepted by CENTCOM. IRGC targeted US AIR BASE at 4:50 AM local time. BRENT: $93.71 Wednesday close (-58 cents) — lowest since mid-March. Rebounding Thursday on fresh fighting. HOCHSTEIN: "No matter what — Iranians will control Hormuz for foreseeable future. Doesn't even matter what the deal says." India Thursday: binary. Trump signs = Brent $85-88, Nifty +800-1,000. Trump rejects = Brent $100+, Nifty -300-400. West Asia War Day 90.

assessment.headline: DAY 101, 9:30AM TUE: MAHSHAHR PETROCHEMICAL COMPLEX HIT (first energy strike since Apr 8 ceasefire). IRAN-ISRAEL APPEAR TO PAUSE. TRUMP: 'BOTH SIDES WANT IMMEDIATE CEASEFIRE.' IRAN WILLING TO STOP IF ISRAEL STOPS. PAKISTAN NAQVI SPECIAL LETTER TO KHAMENEI. NIFTY MON CLOSE 23,123 (-1.04%). BRENT $94.25 CLOSE ($97+ INTRADAY). GIFT NIFTY TUE: -20 pts. MOST POSITIVE DEAL SIGNAL SINCE DAY 86.
assessment.body:
Tuesday 9:30 AM IST. Day 101. The day after the centenary.
The conflict's most dramatic 24 hours — and now, the most positive deal signal in 15 days.

WHAT HAPPENED MONDAY
Iran fired dozens of missiles at Israel — all intercepted.
Israel retaliated: struck Mahshahr petrochemical complex (first energy hit since ceasefire).
Brent spiked to $97.15 intraday (+4.47%).
Nifty fell 244 pts (-1.04%). Sensex -719 pts. BSE -Rs6.31 trillion.
Steepest fall in 2 months.

WHAT HAPPENED NEXT — THE TURNING POINT
Trump posted on Truth Social: "Israel and Iran must immediately stop shooting."
Trump: "Both sides, Israel and Iran, are looking to do an immediate CEASEFIRE!"
Trump: Netanyahu "doesn't call the shots" — rebuked him with obscenities last week.
Iran told Trump admin: willing to stop shooting if Israel does same.
Pakistan PM Shehbaz: "final objective is just about to be achieved."
Pakistan Interior Minister Naqvi: delivered special letter to Khamenei in Tehran.
Iran-Israel appeared to pause strikes (AP, June 8, 4:49 PM ET).
Iran UN ambassador: hopes final agreement soon.
Iran ambassador Moscow: Hormuz will open under Iran-Oman conditions.

MARKET VERDICT
Brent closed at $94.25 — down from $97.15 intraday. Markets believe the pause.
GIFT Nifty Tuesday: 23,157.5 (-20 pts) — vs Monday's -273 gap.
The market is pricing de-escalation, not further escalation.

THE DEAL WINDOW — MOST POSITIVE SINCE DAY 86
Iran willing to stop. Trump pressing Netanyahu hard.
Pakistan mediating actively with Khamenei-level engagement.
Lebanon-Israel ceasefire agreed June 3 (though Hezbollah rejected).
OPEC+ +188k bpd July — limited but positive signal.
The critical unknown: Will Netanyahu hold back?
One more Israeli strike = deal collapses again.
No strike + Iran stands down = deal possible within days.

FOR INDIA AT 9:30AM
GIFT Nifty -20 pts — cautious but not panicked.
Nifty support 23,000-23,100.
LPG Rs941.50 (third hike absorbed).
Brent $94.25 — OMC under-recovery Rs28-32/L diesel at this level.
If deal closes this week: Brent falls to $80-85, Nifty surges 1,000-1,500 pts.
If Mahshahr triggers more exchanges: Brent to $100+, Nifty tests 22,500.

featured.title: The Strait of Hormuz and the New Logic of Chokepoint Control
featured.desc: Chokepoint control is no longer binary (open/closed) but a layered spatial contest spanning seabed topology, island sovereignty, electronic warfare, and visibility asymmetry. The cartography of maritime control in the 2026 crisis.

featured.title: Geopolitics of LPG Supply in India
featured.desc: How India's LPG import dependency on the Gulf creates acute vulnerability during the West Asia War. Explores Hormuz exposure, alternative supply routes, and policy imperatives for energy security in a blockade scenario.

featured.title: Geopolitics of Fertiliser Supply in India
featured.desc: India imports 30%+ of its fertilisers via the Strait of Hormuz. This paper maps the supply chain risks to kharif and rabi crops, the strategic case for diversification, and what a prolonged blockade means for food security.
